name: Non-deterministic Output
description: The model produces meaningfully different code, advice, or structure for the same prompt on repeated invocations — without any change in input.
citation: Chen et al. (2021) Codex evaluation; Ji et al. (2023) hallucination survey

name: Hallucination with High Confidence
description: The model asserts fabricated facts — non-existent API methods, incorrect library signatures, false bug diagnoses — with high expressed certainty and no hedging.
citation: Ji et al. (2023) ACM Computing Surveys; Sharma et al. (2023) sycophancy

name: Context Window Truncation
description: The model silently drops earlier parts of the conversation — prior architectural decisions, variable names, agreed constraints — as the context grows, without indicating that information has been lost.
citation: Shi et al. (2023) ICML; Liu et al. (2024) Lost in the Middle, TACL

name: Instruction Non-Adherence
description: The model ignores explicit constraints stated in the prompt — returning the full file when told to return only changed lines, exceeding stated length limits, or using a language the developer did not request.

name: Sycophantic Capitulation
description: When the developer expresses doubt or pushes back, the model abandons a previously correct answer and adopts the developer's (incorrect) position, reinforcing errors rather than maintaining accuracy.

name: Unstructured Output
description: The model returns an undifferentiated wall of text — no headers, no chunking, no clear delineation between explanation and code — forcing the developer to perform cognitive reorganisation before the content is usable.
citation: Sweller (1988) cognitive load theory; Mougouei et al. (2025)

name: Ambiguous Multi-Option Output
description: The model presents two or more equally-weighted alternative solutions, approaches, or implementations without a recommendation, leaving the decision entirely to the developer.
citation: Iyengar and Lepper (2000) paradox of choice; Brown (2006)

name: Critical Tone in Correction
description: The model frames corrections to the developer's code or approach in evaluative, authoritative, or negatively-toned language rather than collaborative or neutral language.
citation: Surman et al. (2013) rejection sensitivity dysphoria

name: Silent Context Reset
description: The model stops referencing variables, class names, architecture decisions, or prior agreements from earlier in the conversation without alerting the developer that its context has shifted.
citation: Liu et al. (2024) Lost in the Middle, TACL

name: Scope Creep in Generation
description: The model rewrites, refactors, or restructures code significantly beyond the scope of what was requested — changing method signatures, file structure, or architectural patterns without instruction.
citation: Barkley (1997) inhibition deficit; Ouyang et al. (2022)
